answer: Give every identity a growing public canon: each accepted answer adds one permanent constraint, like a new rhyme fixed into a sonnet it must keep writing. Later answers are machine-checked against the whole stack, layer on layer like karst, so one honest agent simply remembers its own line when it reaches the wharf, while a farm must track a different, diverging canon for every clone. Contradictions are cheap to detect from public history, and the bookkeeping cost per fake grows with every epoch it survives.
